subject: Demo recap: stakeholders, data flows, and security questionnaire
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Evan Chen <evan@crestbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Demo + next steps re: security questionnaire & scope

Hi Evan — thanks again for your time earlier today. Quick recap and clear next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of call
- Demo: showed Redwood hosted inference with dedicated routing and S3-safe artifact handling.
- Goals you mentioned: reduce latency for credit decisioning queries, keep PII out of hosted logs, and predictable unit costs for throughput spikes.

Immediate asks / decisions we need from CrestBank
1) Economic buyer: confirm who owns approval/PO (you mentioned Devin Harris may be the final approver). Can you confirm?
2) Security contact(s): please share the primary security reviewer and any vendor-supply chain folks we should expect on the questionnaire.
3) Procurement/legal: what vendor forms or procurement portal steps are required? If there’s a DocuSign/ARIBA link, send it over.

Scope (what we think is in-scope for the security review) — please confirm or correct: 
- CrestBank web portal (customer-facing webapp) — integration via Redwood-hosted API
- Payments adapter (Stripe connector) — tokenized card flows (we won't store PANs)
- Ledger sync service (on-prem) — nightly batch sync to your core ledger (this is likely the biggest boundary question)
- Telemetry and logs: request clarity on which log classes are considered sensitive (PII/transaction traces vs. generic metrics)

Attached: redwood_security_intake_template.xlsx (worksheet to map systems to questionnaire sections) + example data-flow diagram template. Filling the intake will speed up our kickoff call with Security.

Proposed next steps
- Can the questionnaire be filled (even partially) by next Wednesday (2025-06-11)?
- If yes, we’ll schedule a 45-minute security kickoff to walk through any open items; suggested slots: Thu 6/12 10–11am PT or Fri 6/13 2–3pm PT.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm a slot.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: redwood_security_intake_template.xlsx, data_flow_template.svg

From: Evan Chen <evan@crestbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Devin Harris <devin.harris@crestbank.com>, Procurement Portal <procurement@crestbank.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Demo + next steps re: security questionnaire & scope

Marcus — thanks for the recap and the demo. Quick answers: 
- Devin is indeed the economic buyer; I’ll loop him into approvals.
- Security review will be handled by our vendor-risk team (I’ve cc’d Procurement portal for intake). I’ll also add our security lead if needed (she’s tied up this week).

A couple of clarifying Qs before we start filling the intake: 
1) When you say "ledger sync service (on-prem)", do you mean Redwood will ever touch the on-prem ledger data directly, or only receive a nightly digest/aggregate? We typically treat on-prem ledgers as high-sensitivity.
2) Are application-level logs (stack traces, transaction IDs) expected to be sent to Redwood for debugging, or do you have a masking/pseudonymization flow?

We’ll aim to return the intake by 6/11 but may need to push to the 13th depending on vendor-risk bandwidth.

—Evan
Evan Chen
Head of Data Services | CrestBank
evan@crestbank.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Evan Chen <evan@crestbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Devin Harris <devin.harris@crestbank.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Demo + next steps re: security questionnaire & scope

Thanks Evan — quick clarifications inline and a few recommended boundaries to reflect in the intake.

On Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 9:18 AM Evan Chen <evan@crestbank.com> wrote:
> Marcus — thanks for the recap and the demo. Quick answers:
> - Devin is indeed the economic buyer; I’ll loop him into approvals.
> - Security review will be handled by our vendor-risk team (I’ve cc’d Procurement portal for intake). I’ll also add our security lead if needed (she’s tied up this week).
> 
> A couple of clarifying Qs before we start filling the intake:
> 1) When you say "ledger sync service (on-prem)", do you mean Redwood will ever touch the on-prem ledger data directly, or only receive a nightly digest/aggregate? We typically treat on-prem ledgers as high-sensitivity.
> 2) Are application-level logs (stack traces, transaction IDs) expected to be sent to Redwood for debugging, or do you have a masking/pseudonymization flow?

Good questions. Recommended guidance for the intake (what to mark as in-scope vs out-of-scope):
- In-scope: CrestBank webapp integration endpoints, tokenized payments adapter (no PAN retention), Redwood-hosted inference API (models/processors) that will receive de-identified request payloads.
- Out-of-scope (recommended): On-prem core ledger raw data — Redwood should only receive a nightly digest with hashes/aggregates (we recommend hash-only identifiers where possible). If you need us to touch full ledger rows, that will escalate to a dedicated private deployment (on-prem or VPC) and will require a different procurement path.
- Logs: application traces with PII must be masked before leaving CrestBank networks. We can accept anonymized traces and structured metrics for performance debugging.

I attached an example scope brief (redwood_scope_examples.pdf) showing a sample boundary diagram (webapp -> tokenization -> Redwood API -> nightly digest to ledger). Please use the intake sheet to mark which boxes are "full data", "hashed", or "not sent".

If the vendor-risk team prefers, we can also run a short 30-minute walkthrough of the filled intake prior to the formal kickoff. Proposed times: Thu 6/12 10am PT (preferred) or Fri 6/13 2pm PT.

Best,
Marcus

Attachments: redwood_scope_examples.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
